question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0\,\text{or}\,y<0 \\ \frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & 0\le x\le 2,\,y>1 \\ {F}_{Y}(y), & x>2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 1, & x>2,\,y>1.\end{aligned}
$$

where ${F}_{X}$ and ${F}_{Y}$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ is determined by

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y).
$$

For $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3/2})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{y}^{1/2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{y}^{1/2}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{3}{4}x{y}^{1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y)=0.$
Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x{y}^{1/2}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
